name: UC Davis School of Medicine
notes: Regional connection to Northern or Central California matters enough to have its own short-answer prompt.

prompts.title: Application Concerns
prompts.text: Discuss any elements of your application that you feel might be concerning to the Admissions Committee (This could include explanation of metric trends, institutional actions, legal violations, etc.) Please enter N/A if no concerns to report.

prompts.title: Regional Connection
prompts.text: Do you have a connection to Northern or Central California?

prompts.title: UC Davis-Relevant Activities
prompts.limit: 1500 characters each for up to 3 activities
prompts.text: Please list the activities you would like to be considered in your application to UC Davis. The secondary activities may be used to highlight your experiences specifically relevant for UC Davis. Please only list three. Briefly describe each activity and its significance. How did it prepare you for a medical career?

name: University of California San Diego School of Medicine
notes: Large set with several program-specific prompts. Keep only the ones relevant to the programs you are actually applying to.

prompts.title: Autobiographical Statement
prompts.text: This should be a true autobiographical statement. Topics to be included are family, childhood, primary and secondary school years, undergraduate years, and, if applicable, what you’ve done since completing your bachelor’s degree. You should also discuss the motivational factors which led you to a career in medicine, including any disadvantages or obstacles which might put your accomplishments into context.

prompts.title: PRIME-HEq
prompts.text: For PRIME-HEq: Please describe your interest in the PRIME-HEq program.

prompts.title: Global Health
prompts.text: For GHAC: Please describe your interest in Global Health.

prompts.title: PRIME-TIDE
prompts.text: For PRIME-TIDE: Describe your interest in the Program in Medicine - Transforming Indigenous Doctor Education.

prompts.title: Tan Family Scholar Program
prompts.text: For the Tan Family Scholar Program: Please describe your interest in Compassion and Empathy.

prompts.title: Marginalization and Disparity
prompts.text: Do you consider yourself to be a member of a group that is marginalized in a way that systemically affects access to quality education or healthcare? Please describe how educational disparity, health disparity and/or marginalization has impacted you and your community.

prompts.title: Additional Most Meaningful Activities
prompts.text: In addition to the three most meaningful experiences on AMCAS, are there any additional activities you would consider among your most meaningful?

prompts.title: Career Pathway
prompts.text: Please select a potential career pathway and provide a brief description of your future career goals.

name: Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine
secondary_cycle: Latest public prompt set found on Bright Doctor as of 2026-04-18
notes: Prompt source is not Admit.org because the Admit prompt page was not surfaced cleanly in search results. Bright Doctor also reports no CASPer/PREview requirement on the captured guide page.

prompts.title: Unfavorable Outcome
prompts.text: During your career as a physician, you will potentially encounter obstacles, and be required to overcome challenges. Please describe your experience with a situation that had an unfavorable outcome, including your reaction, how you might have responded differently, and what you learned about yourself.

prompts.title: Diversity Contribution
prompts.text: Kaiser Permanente is committed to advancing equity, inclusion, and diversity for all. How will you contribute to the diversity of the Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine?

prompts.title: Lifelong Learning
prompts.text: Lifelong learning is an essential process for continued professional development. Please tell us about an area of intellectual exploration you’re passionate about, and your approach to exploring this area.

prompts.title: COVID Impact
prompts.text: Optional: Please describe how you have been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: Keck School of Medicine of USC
notes: Very short answers. Tone and precision matter more than exposition.

prompts.title: Fun Lately
prompts.text: What is the most fun you’ve had lately?

prompts.title: Nickname
prompts.text: If you had to give yourself a nickname, what would it be?

prompts.title: Three Things You Don't Care About
prompts.text: What are three things you don't care about at all?

prompts.title: Didn't Get What You Deserved
prompts.text: Describe a situation in which you didn’t get something you felt you deserved.

prompts.title: Anything Else
prompts.text: Is there anything else you would like us to know?

prompts.title: Prior Medical School Application
prompts.text: Have you previously applied to or attended medical school? If yes, please provide an explanation on what occurred with your application process or previous matriculation to medical school.

name: University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry
notes: Only one prompt in the latest Admit.org archive, centered on community.

prompts.title: Community
prompts.text: Involvement in community is one of the pillars of the University of Rochester School of Medicine education. Tell us about a community you identify with and how you are involved with it.

name: University of Colorado School of Medicine
notes: Includes branch-program prompts; keep only the ones relevant to the tracks you actually select.

prompts.title: Leadership / Curiosity / Commitment
prompts.text: The pillars of our curriculum are Leadership, Curiosity, and Commitment. Tell us about how you have embodied one or more of these attributes in your path to medicine thus far. In which of these areas do you see the most opportunity for personal growth and why?

prompts.title: Inclusive Excellence
prompts.text: Please describe how your background and/or your unique lived experiences contribute to our culture of inclusive excellence.

prompts.title: Fort Collins Branch
prompts.text: Fort Collins Branch: Please tell us why you are interested in being a part of the 4-year CUSOM at CSU (Fort Collins Branch campus).

prompts.title: Rural Branch
prompts.text: Rural Branch: Why are you interested in being a rural physician? How will rural life and work fit your personal goals?

prompts.title: Aerospace Engineering Dual Degree
prompts.text: Aerospace engineering dual degree: Describe your career path up to this point and how that has led to your interest in human spaceflight.

prompts.title: Colorado Springs Branch
prompts.text: Colorado Springs Branch: Please submit a short statement regarding your interest in the Colorado Springs Branch.

name: Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University
notes: Campus-specific prompt means your selected program location should shape the school-fit draft.

prompts.title: Why Temple
prompts.text: What is the nature of your interest in the Lewis Katz School of Medicine?

prompts.title: What Makes You Unique
prompts.text: Describe what makes you unique as an applicant, an obstacle that you had to overcome, or how you will contribute to the Katz community.

prompts.title: Campus Interest
prompts.text: Tell us about your special interest in the campus you selected.

prompts.title: Current Year Plans
prompts.text: What are your plans for the current year?

prompts.title: COVID Impact
prompts.text: Please use this space to describe to us how you were impacted academically, personally or professionally by COVID-19.

name: Emory University School of Medicine
notes: Short limits; concise storytelling matters more than background exposition.

prompts.title: Curriculum / Current Year Plan
prompts.text: List your entire curriculum plan for the academic year. If you are not in school, briefly describe your plans for the coming year.

prompts.title: Health-Related Experiences
prompts.text: Briefly describe your health-related experiences. Be sure to include important experiences that are in your AMCAS application, as well as any recent experiences.

prompts.title: Why Emory
prompts.text: Briefly describe your interest in Emory and the Emory degree program you have selected.

prompts.title: Service to Underserved Communities
prompts.text: Please describe any of your activities that have been in service to under-served communities.

prompts.title: Updates
prompts.text: If you have any updates or new information to report since you have submitted your AMCAS primary application, please briefly describe below.

name: University of Cincinnati College of Medicine
notes: This is one of the more extensive secondary sets on your list.

prompts.title: Traffic Violations
prompts.text: Have you ever been convicted of or pled guilty or no contest to any moving traffic violations? If yes, please explain fully below.

prompts.title: Matriculation-Year Plans
prompts.text: Provide a thorough explanation of all activities planned between now and your matriculation into medical school.

prompts.title: Patient-Centered Care and Diversity
prompts.text: Consider an experience in which you collaborated or were exposed to diverse backgrounds that would inform your own vision for patient-centered care. Please describe the impact the experience had on you.

prompts.title: Teamwork
prompts.text: What does teamwork mean to you? What teamwork experiences have you had? How do you navigate your role and the role of other team members?

prompts.title: Application Concerns
prompts.text: Discuss any elements of your application that you feel might be concerning to the Admissions Committee.

prompts.title: Why UCCOM
prompts.text: What is your specific interest in the UCCOM program? What opportunities would you take advantage of as a student here? Why?

prompts.title: Academic Breadth
prompts.text: How has your academic work beyond the traditional pre-medical requirements prepared you for medical school and for a career in medicine? Please highlight any service-learning activities that you have done.

prompts.title: Interview Preference
prompts.text: If invited to interview, indicate your interview preference and briefly explain it.

name: Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth
notes: The Geisel prompts let you reuse current-year plans, why-school, additional-info, and social-justice backbones.

prompts.title: Current Year Plans
prompts.text: Please indicate your plans for the academic year. If in school, please list your courses. If working, let us know something about the nature of your job.

prompts.title: Helpful Context
prompts.text: Please reflect on your primary application and share something not addressed elsewhere that would be helpful to the Admissions Committee as we review your file.

prompts.title: Why Geisel
prompts.text: What aspects of the Geisel School of Medicine draw you to apply? Please include the characteristics and strengths you will bring to our program and how you hope to contribute to our community.

prompts.title: Being the Other
prompts.text: Geisel School of Medicine values social justice and diversity in all its forms. Reflect on a situation where you were the 'other'.

name: Tufts University School of Medicine
notes: Tufts has a large prompt set but much of it maps cleanly to shared backbones.

prompts.title: Why Tufts
prompts.text: Do you wish to share a specific reason why have you chosen to apply to Tufts University School of Medicine?

prompts.title: Coming Year Plans
prompts.text: Please briefly describe your plans for the coming year.

prompts.title: Journey to Medicine
prompts.text: Please tell us about your journey to medical school and how your background and experiences will positively impact your future as a medical student and physician.

prompts.title: Clinical Experience
prompts.text: Which of your experiences with clinical medicine or healthcare has best prepared you for a future career as a physician, and why?

prompts.title: Social Responsibility
prompts.text: Have you done substantial work or service that has contributed to societal good, or addressed social determinants of health, health equity, or social justice?

prompts.title: Withdrawals / Repeats
prompts.text: Do you have any withdrawals or repeated coursework listed on your transcript(s)?

prompts.title: Leaves / Breaks
prompts.text: Did you take any leaves of absence or significant breaks from your undergraduate education?

prompts.title: Academic Challenges
prompts.text: We encourage you to use this space to elaborate on any academic challenges you have overcome since completing high school.

name: The Ohio State University College of Medicine
notes: Track-specific prompts only matter if you apply to those tracks.

prompts.title: Mission Areas
prompts.text: The mission statement of The Ohio State University College of Medicine is to improve people's lives through innovation in research, medical education, and patient care. Please describe how your past experiences predict your potential to contribute in two of these three areas.

prompts.title: Health Inequities
prompts.text: Provide examples of factors contributing to health inequities that exist in the United States.

prompts.title: Primary Care Track Readiness
prompts.text: Primary Care Track: How do you feel ready to choose a career in family medicine? Please provide any examples of exposure and/or experiences not already mentioned in your application.

prompts.title: Primary Care Track Rationale
prompts.text: Primary Care Track: Describe your rationale for wanting to pursue an accelerated curriculum in preparation for a career in family medicine.

prompts.title: Community Medicine Track Rationale
prompts.text: Community Medicine Track: Describe your rationale for wanting to pursue an accelerated curriculum in preparation for a career in family medicine.

prompts.title: Community Training Interest
prompts.text: Community Medicine Track: Why are you interested in training in a smaller community, and what is the impact you hope to have by training in this setting?

name: Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine
notes: Several short explanatory prompts; good candidate for concise reusable context blocks.

prompts.title: Direct to College
prompts.text: Did you go on to college directly after high school?

prompts.title: Direct to Medical School / Gap Years
prompts.text: Are you expecting to go on to medical school directly after completing your undergraduate degree? If you took gap year(s), please use this space to explain what you have been doing prior to applying to medical school.

prompts.title: More Than Four Years Undergraduate
prompts.text: If you have spent more than 4 years as an undergraduate, please explain below.

prompts.title: Educational Narrative / Timeline
prompts.text: Please provide a narrative or timeline to describe any features of your educational history that you think may be of particular interest to us.

prompts.title: Additional Strengths
prompts.text: Use the space below to provide additional information you feel will provide us with a comprehensive understanding of your strengths as a candidate for a career in medicine.

prompts.title: Safety Net Environment
prompts.text: Boston Medical Center is the largest safety net hospital in New England. Why are you specifically interested in beginning your medical education in this environment, and how do you feel that your previous experiences will prepare you for this unique learning environment?

name: Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine
secondary_cycle: 2025-2026 from ProspectiveDoctor / Med School Insiders / Virginia Tech admissions page
notes: Current official page says 2026-2027 prompts will be posted in summer 2026. This workspace uses the latest public 2025-2026 prompt set.

prompts.title: Fictional Character
prompts.text: Who is a fictional character that is similar to you? Describe a time when you embodied that character.

prompts.title: Humility
prompts.text: What can a recovering addict who didn’t finish high school teach their physician?

prompts.title: Being Corrected
prompts.text: Describe a time (not related to research) when you were told you had done something wrong. How has the experience changed you?

prompts.title: Publications
prompts.text: Please list any publications in the appropriate citation format using the text box below.

name: University of Virginia School of Medicine
notes: Using the latest public 2025-2026 prompt set surfaced in search results rather than the older Admit archive page.

prompts.title: Why UVA
prompts.text: Why are you interested in attending the University of Virginia School of Medicine? What factors will be most important to you in choosing a medical school?

prompts.title: Challenge or Obstacle
prompts.text: Tell us about a challenge or obstacle you experienced. How did you manage it?

prompts.title: Pandemic Impact
prompts.text: Please briefly describe how the pandemic impacted your ability to pursue experiences like clinical work, shadowing, research, or community service.

prompts.title: Future Activities
prompts.text: Please list any and all future activities in clinical work, shadowing, research, or community service that you plan to pursue in the upcoming year.

name: Vermont Larner College of Medicine
notes: Prompt set is strongly mission-and-curriculum specific.

prompts.title: Active Learning Fit
prompts.text: The Larner College of Medicine curriculum emphasizes active in-person participation and peer co-learning. Please share your thoughts on the suitability of active learning for you.

prompts.title: Learning Across Difference
prompts.text: Reflect on a time you learned something from someone or a group of people who are unlike yourself and how that challenged your preconceptions or biases. How will this experience influence your behavior in the future?

prompts.title: Professionalism
prompts.text: How has your understanding of what professionalism means evolved over time? Reflect on a personal experience that contributed to your understanding of your own core values.

prompts.title: Why Larner
prompts.text: What unique opportunities at Larner College of Medicine would be meaningful to you in your education and how do these align with your larger goal of becoming a physician?

prompts.title: Additional Information
prompts.text: Use this space to share any information, not presented elsewhere, that will clarify any aspect of your application. If you are a reapplicant, you may choose to share what you have done since your previous application.

name: University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health
notes: Very mission-forward; strong prompt overlap with competency, equity, and fit essays.

prompts.title: Mission Fit
prompts.text: The Admissions Committee is committed to holistic, mission-aligned evaluation of all applicants. Review our institution’s mission. Using specific examples, discuss how and why you believe you are a good fit for the University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health.

prompts.title: Competency 1
prompts.text: Choose one of the professional competencies that has been a point of pride or emphasis on your path to medical school. Using specific examples, describe how you have demonstrated it in your experiences to date.

prompts.title: Competency 2
prompts.text: Choose a different professional competency that has been another point of pride or emphasis. Using specific examples, describe how you have demonstrated this one in your experiences to date.

prompts.title: Health Equity Issue
prompts.text: Choose a broader issue or policy that impacts health outcomes where you believe change is needed to advance health equity. Discuss the role you hope to play as a physician in addressing this issue.

prompts.title: COVID Impact
prompts.text: In a paragraph, please share how COVID-19 impacted your application in any of the following domains: academic, volunteer, research, work, personal life.

name: Medical College of Wisconsin
notes: Strong overlap with diversity, school-fit, regret, and health equity themes.

prompts.title: Contribution to MCW
prompts.text: Explain how your unique background, identity, interests, or talents will contribute to the MCW community.

prompts.title: Why MCW
prompts.text: How will MCW uniquely prepare you for your future goals?

prompts.title: Decision You Regret
prompts.text: Recount a time when you made a decision you regret. How did it affect you, and what did you learn from the experience?

prompts.title: Health Equity
prompts.text: Share what you have learned or how you have grown through working with or serving people from cultural backgrounds or groups different than your own. How do you believe you can contribute to improving health equity or reducing health disparities as a physician?

prompts.title: Reapplicant
prompts.text: Reapplicant: Please explain how your application has changed since your last application to MCW Medical School.

name: Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University
notes: Only two prompts, so the diversity essay carries a lot of weight.

prompts.title: Diversity Contribution
prompts.text: Sidney Kimmel Medical College defines diversity as the richness in human differences. How will your own experiences allow you to contribute to the diversity of the student body and to provide equitable and inclusive care to your future patients?

prompts.title: Additional Information
prompts.text: Do you have additional information that you would like to provide at this time?

name: University of Iowa Roy J. and Lucille A. Carver College of Medicine
notes: Two of these prompts are especially useful to sync with your why-school and uniqueness backbones.

prompts.title: Why Carver
prompts.text: We understand you may be applying to multiple medical schools. Please explain your reasons for applying to the Carver College of Medicine.

prompts.title: Unique Characteristic
prompts.text: Describe a personal characteristic, challenge, or experience that makes you unique. How will this influence your contribution to a dynamic healthcare system that advocates for all peoples?

prompts.title: Medically Related Experiences
prompts.text: Please list and briefly describe all medically related experiences (paid/volunteer) you have completed during the past 5 years.

prompts.title: Reapplicant
prompts.text: If you are a reapplicant to the Carver College of Medicine, how have you strengthened your application?

prompts.title: If Not in Degree Program
prompts.text: If you are not currently in a degree-seeking program, please indicate what you will be doing from the time you complete this secondary application to the start of medical school.

name: Western Michigan University Homer Stryker M.D. School of Medicine
notes: Strong focus on WMed-specific fit plus regional connection.

prompts.title: Why WMed
prompts.text: Please explain both of the following: the specific reason(s) you have chosen to apply to WMed and how you will utilize the unique features of WMed's mission, vision, and curriculum to achieve your career goals.

prompts.title: Diversity Contribution
prompts.text: Describe how you add to the cultural, ethnic, and socioeconomic diversity of the medical profession and what you bring to the practice of medicine.

prompts.title: Reapplicant
prompts.text: WMed re-applicants only: Describe the changes to your application from previous cycles.

prompts.title: Southwest Michigan Connection
prompts.text: Please explain any connection you have to Southwest Michigan.

prompts.title: Additional Information
prompts.text: Is there any additional information not included elsewhere in your application you would like the admissions committee to know?

name: University of Miami Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine
notes: Prompt text below reflects the search snippet surfaced from Admit.org on 2026-04-18.

prompts.title: Why Miami
prompts.text: Why are you applying to the University of Miami Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine? Please provide a response that clearly articulates how you believe our program specifically will enhance your education/training, what you feel you will uniquely contribute to our learning community, and/or what features of our medical school prompted you to apply.

prompts.title: Diverse Environments
prompts.text: Please discuss any experiences you may have had serving, working, living, and/or learning in broadly diverse environments that you believe would enable you to thrive in and contribute to our Miller SOM and Greater Miami community.

prompts.title: Values
prompts.text: Please discuss how your experiences align with core values such as integrity, collaboration, accountability, respect, and excellence.

name: Wake Forest University School of Medicine
secondary_cycle: 2024-2025 complete prompt set from Med School Insiders page find result
notes: I could verify the full 2024-2025 set from page text. The same page also shows a newer cycle, but the full newer prompt list was not cleanly extractable from the search tool.

prompts.title: Promote Equity
prompts.text: Consider your abilities, insights, and previous experiences and then tell us about your ability to promote equity.

prompts.title: Non-Academic Challenge
prompts.text: Describe a non-academic challenge you have faced and explain how you overcame it.

prompts.title: Most Formative Experience
prompts.text: From your list of most meaningful experiences on the AMCAS application, choose one that has been the most formative in terms of your desire for a career in medicine. Why did that experience have such meaning for you in your decision-making process?

prompts.title: Collaboration
prompts.text: Please share an experience that demonstrates how you have collaborated with others.

prompts.title: Future Goals
prompts.text: Describe your future goal(s). Reflect on your past experiences and describe how these experiences will shape your goal(s).

prompts.title: Why Wake Forest
prompts.text: Tell us about any specific reason(s) (personal, educational, etc.) why you see yourself here at the Wake Forest University School of Medicine.

prompts.title: Interesting Fact
prompts.text: Please tell us an interesting fact about yourself that a casual acquaintance may find surprising or interesting.

name: Albany Medical College
notes: Large prompt set with strong overlap in challenge, community, and social-determinants essays.

prompts.title: Describe Yourself
prompts.text: Describe yourself.

prompts.title: Academic Inconsistencies
prompts.text: Please explain any inconsistencies in your university, graduate, or professional school academic performance and/or MCAT scores. If the question does not apply to you, please put N/A in the box provided.

prompts.title: Interrupted Attendance or Gaps
prompts.text: Has your college or university, graduate or professional school attendance been interrupted for any reason? If yes, please explain. Also, please explain any extended gaps in activity/employment in your post-graduate history. If the question does not apply to you, please put N/A in the box provided.

prompts.title: Significant Challenge
prompts.text: Describe a significant challenge that has prepared you for the MD career path.

prompts.title: Structural and Social Determinants of Health
prompts.text: Please describe your personal experiences with the structural and social determinants of health in your life and community, how they shaped your engagement with medicine and your future ideas for doctoring.

prompts.title: Community Identity
prompts.text: Tell us about a community with which you identify and how you are involved with it.

prompts.title: Anything Else
prompts.text: Is there anything else you would like the admissions committee to know when reviewing your application? If so, please use the space provided.

prompts.title: Most Meaningful Activity Impact
prompts.text: In the Work and Activities section on your AMCAS application, select the experience that has been the most meaningful in influencing your desire to pursue a career in medicine, explain why, and describe what aspect of that experience best equips you to make an impact in the medical profession.

name: Drexel University College of Medicine
notes: Compact prompt set with direct overlap across why-school, current-year, and context essays.

prompts.title: Current and Recent Activities
prompts.text: Please discuss all of your current and recent activities and engagements that have prepared you for medical school. Please be sure to include any traditional and/or non-traditional clinical exposures and volunteering experiences that you have done that are not already included in your application.

prompts.title: Why Drexel and Mission Fit
prompts.text: Why are you interested in Drexel? Please also explain how you meet various elements of our mission - compassionate care, diversity, spirited inquiry, collaboration, and opportunity.

prompts.title: Extenuating Circumstances
prompts.text: Please describe any extenuating circumstances that may have affected your medical or non-medical service experiences, including any circumstances that impacted your engagement in activities, academics, and MCAT that would have helped to prepare you for medical school.

name: Wayne State University School of Medicine
secondary_deadline: Advised within 2 weeks of request; final deadline February 8, 2026
notes: Urban mission and belonging prompts line up especially well with service, justice, and community work.

prompts.title: Motivation and Challenges of Medicine
prompts.text: When reflecting on the roles and responsibilities of a physician, please discuss what motivated your interest. What are potential challenges to pursuing a career in medicine?

prompts.title: Healthcare Challenges in Under-Resourced Communities
prompts.text: What are the healthcare challenges faced by under-resourced communities in the U.S.? Why do these healthcare challenges exist? How would you address them?

prompts.title: Mission Alignment
prompts.text: Which of your experiences and activities align with WSU SOM's mission? Please discuss how they align.

prompts.title: Belonging and Class Contribution
prompts.text: The Wayne State University School of Medicine aims to provide a rich, varied, and inclusive educational experience for all members of the class. How would you advance belonging and contribute to the educational experience of fellow medical students?

prompts.title: Growth Year
prompts.text: Please answer if you have had a gap or growth year (career change, re-applicant, additional education, etc.). A growth year is defined as a period of time between the end of your undergraduate education and a year or more prior to the start of medical school. What activities have you participated in or plan to participate in during this period? How does this relate to your future career in medicine?

name: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine
notes: Prompt set centers on Jesuit mission, social justice, service, disagreement, and professional challenge.

prompts.title: Jesuit Mission Resonance
prompts.text: As you consider Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine, please tell us what resonates with you regarding our mission as a Jesuit, Catholic medical school? Consider also what you may be curious about regarding our institutional mission and identity.

prompts.title: Why Medicine
prompts.text: Considering all that you could do with your life, how have you discerned your decision to become a physician? What is particular to the practice of medicine and the vocation of a physician that draws you to apply to medical school versus another helping/caring profession? What experiences, conversations, and encounters have informed your decision to apply?

prompts.title: Social Justice and Under-Resourced Communities
prompts.text: Social justice, in the Jesuit tradition, justice due to each person's inherent human dignity, is an essential dimension of education at SSOM. Describe an impactful experience working with and for under-resourced communities. Explain what you have learned about yourself through this service and/or what has hindered your efforts to serve others in these environments.

prompts.title: Disagreeing with Feedback
prompts.text: Describe a time you received feedback about your performance and disagreed with the feedback. What did you disagree with? How did you handle it?

prompts.title: Non-Academic Challenge or Conflict
prompts.text: Describe a non-academic personal/professional challenge or conflict that you have experienced. Explain what skills, resources and/or strategies you employed to resolve the problem.

prompts.title: Updates and Context
prompts.text: Please indicate additional grades earned, amendments to your proposed coursework or graduation date, address changes, additions to your list of experiences, and anything else you feel we should know.

prompts.title: Gaps, Delays, or Academic Missteps
prompts.text: Please explain in more detail anything that would help us understand any gaps or delays in your education, academic missteps, or personal challenges not listed elsewhere.

prompts.title: If Out of Coursework for Two Years
prompts.text: If you have not been enrolled in coursework for over two years, please let us know what you have been doing since your coursework ended.

prompts.title: Reapplicant Improvement
prompts.text: Have you applied to SSOM prior to this application? If so, please list the years of your previous application submissions to SSOM and tell us how your application has improved since your previous submission.

name: Frank H. Netter M.D. School of Medicine at Quinnipiac University
notes: Strong overlap across gap-year, lived-experience, uncertainty, service, and academic context prompts.

prompts.title: Application Year Plan
prompts.text: If you will not be enrolled as a full-time student, how will you be spending or intend to spend your time during your application year? If you are a re-applicant, please address steps taken to improve your application for medical school.

prompts.title: Specialty Interests and Future Career
prompts.text: Although your interests may change, how do you currently envision your specialty interests and future career in medicine and why?

prompts.title: Lived Experiences and Patient Care
prompts.text: Tell us about your lived experiences that will enable you to provide quality care to all patients.

prompts.title: Beyond Your Capabilities
prompts.text: As a medical student and future physician, you will be faced with many uncertain situations. Please describe a situation when you were asked to do something that was beyond your capabilities. How did you handle the situation? Please provide a specific example.

prompts.title: Service with People from Different Backgrounds
prompts.text: At Netter SOM, we value service to each other and others in the community. Please share how you have made efforts to work with people from a different background than you. What did you learn from these efforts?

prompts.title: Withdrawals or Breaks
prompts.text: If applicable, please address any withdrawals, repeated courses, leaves of absence or breaks in your undergraduate education that are not explained in your application.

name: Tulane University School of Medicine
notes: Short prompts; useful to keep concise reusable blocks for why-school, New Orleans fit, leadership, and hobbies.

prompts.title: Why Tulane
prompts.text: Tulane University School of Medicine's mission statement states: We improve human health and foster healthy communities through discovery and translation of the best science into clinical practice and education; to deliver the highest quality patient care and prepare the next generation of distinguished clinical and scientific leaders. Briefly describe the reasons for your interest in Tulane University School of Medicine.

prompts.title: New Orleans Health Disparities
prompts.text: What disparities in health do you believe are pertinent to the New Orleans patient population? How would you attempt to address them as a medical student at Tulane? You may support your answer by using past involvement working in a similar patient population to compare and/or describe your interest in any student activities offered at Tulane or in New Orleans.

prompts.title: How Others Describe You
prompts.text: Who knows you best and how would they describe you?

prompts.title: Leadership Positions
prompts.text: Please list any leadership positions (clubs, organizations, paid work) you may have held.

prompts.title: Hobbies and Interests
prompts.text: Please list your hobbies and major non-academic interests.

prompts.title: Underrepresented Group
prompts.text: Tulane University School of Medicine values the diversity of its patients, faculty, staff, and students. Do you identify with a particular group that you believe is underrepresented among medical professionals?

prompts.title: COVID Impact
prompts.text: In what ways did the COVID-19 pandemic alter or interrupt your medical school application?

name: Eastern Virginia Medical School
notes: Directly aligned to exposure to medicine, future self, and school-specific rationale.

prompts.title: Exposure to Medicine
prompts.text: Briefly describe your exposure to medicine.

prompts.title: What You Will Like Best About Being a Physician
prompts.text: What do you think you will like best about being a physician?

prompts.title: What You Will Like Least About Being a Physician
prompts.text: What do you think you will like least about being a physician?

prompts.title: Ten Years from Now
prompts.text: Describe yourself and your medical career as you see it ten years from now.

prompts.title: Why EVMS
prompts.text: Please indicate your reasons for applying to VHS-EVMS at ODU.

name: Rush Medical College at Rush University
notes: Current prompt set emphasizes worldview, distance traveled, challenge, and health equity.

prompts.title: Worldview and Understanding Difference
prompts.text: Rush Medical College is located on Chicago's Near West Side and serves a diverse patient population. We seek to train physicians who can connect with diverse patient populations with whom they may not share a similar background. Tell us about a life experience that has broadened your own world view or enhanced your ability to understand those unlike yourself and what you learned from this experience.

prompts.title: Distance Traveled - Adversities
prompts.text: Distance traveled is the metaphorical distance that represents the journey an applicant undertakes throughout their life, encompassing achievements, personal identity, and the competencies developed along the way. Based on your experiences and your distance traveled, please describe any adversities, challenges, and/or marginalized experiences that you have encountered. Optional.

prompts.title: Distance Traveled - Effect and Growth
prompts.text: Please describe the effect of these adversities, challenges, and/or marginalized experiences on you as an individual. Explain how you overcame them, what skills you built, what lessons you learned, and how these experiences motivated you to be a doctor. Optional.

prompts.title: Privilege and Health Equity
prompts.text: Can you describe a time when you recognized your privilege and used it to promote health equity? Please share specific initiatives, projects, or actions in which you were involved in and the impact they had. Optional.

name: Chicago Medical School at Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science
notes: Very concise 150-word essays; useful to draft as tight vignettes instead of traditional long-form secondaries.

prompts.title: Why Medicine
prompts.text: What inspired you to pursue a career in medicine, and how have your personal experiences or background shaped your desire to become a physician?

prompts.title: Challenge or Setback
prompts.text: Tell us about a time when you faced a significant challenge or setback. How did you navigate it, and what did you learn from the experience that will help you succeed in medical school?

prompts.title: Empathy in Difficult Times
prompts.text: Describe an experience where you helped someone who was going through a difficult time. How did you approach the situation, and what did you learn about the importance of empathy in providing care?

prompts.title: Self-Consciousness and Growth
prompts.text: Is there anything about yourself that you feel self-conscious about? How have you addressed it, and what have you learned about yourself through this process?

prompts.title: Two Passions
prompts.text: What are two causes or activities you are most passionate about? How do these passions reflect your values and goals as a future physician?

prompts.title: Optional DEI Statement
prompts.text: Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science continuously strives to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI). Each applicant's lived experience provides an opportunity to contribute to our mission. Please share the ways in which your personal experiences, values, qualities and perspectives will enrich RFU and our community. Optional.

name: New York Medical College
notes: Secondary is mostly attestation and context oriented rather than classic narrative essays.

prompts.title: Family Connection
prompts.text: If you have family members with a connection to NYMC as alumni, faculty, or employees of the School of Medicine, indicate the relationship and applicable connection details.

prompts.title: Social Media Policy Explanation
prompts.text: Please review the NYMC Social Media Policy. If you select YES, we ask that you briefly explain what has been posted.

prompts.title: COVID Disruptions
prompts.text: Please share any disruptions in your academic, volunteer, work, and/or personal life related to COVID-19 that you would like the Admissions Committee to consider.

prompts.title: Technical Standards Attestation
prompts.text: Please review the NYMC Technical Standards on the admissions website and attest to your understanding of them.

name: University of California, Riverside School of Medicine
notes: Mission-forward and strongly regional; these drafts should explicitly mention underserved Inland Southern California where appropriate.

prompts.title: Mission Fit and Class Contribution
prompts.text: The mission of the UCR School of Medicine is to improve the health of the people of California and, especially, to serve Inland Southern California by training a diverse workforce of physicians and by developing innovative research and health care delivery programs that will improve the health of the medically underserved in the region and become models to be emulated throughout the state and nation. What experiences, skills, and abilities will you bring to the class to fulfill this mission?

prompts.title: School Value in Practice
prompts.text: The values of the UCR SOM are integrity, innovation, inclusion, excellence, accountability and respect. Please choose one of the values and tell us how you have personally experienced it or have seen it emulated in a clinical setting.

prompts.title: Future Healthcare Setting
prompts.text: In what type of healthcare setting do you see yourself practicing medicine?

prompts.title: Personal Challenge, Resilience, and Grit
prompts.text: Tell us about a personal challenge you have faced in your life thus far and how you demonstrated resilience and grit to overcome it. Please do not write about studying for or taking the MCAT.

prompts.title: Anything Else
prompts.text: If there is anything you would like the committee to consider about your candidacy that is not explained elsewhere in your application, please use this space to tell us.

name: California University of Science and Medicine
notes: Very short prompts; best handled as polished mini-essays with clean thematic separation.

prompts.title: Diversity Contribution
prompts.text: Diversity comes in many forms. How do you think you might contribute to the diversity of the class?

prompts.title: Criticism
prompts.text: Describe the last time you were criticized by a peer or supervisor. How did you handle it?

prompts.title: Working with a Difficult Person
prompts.text: Give an example of when you had to work with someone who was difficult to get along with. Why was this person difficult? How did you handle that person?

prompts.title: Integrity
prompts.text: What would be the best example that shows you are a person of integrity?

prompts.title: Ten Years from Now
prompts.text: If given the opportunity to attend medical school, where would you see yourself in ten years?

prompts.title: Underloaded Terms Explanation
prompts.text: If you were enrolled in fewer than 12 units or credits for more than 1 semester or 2 quarters during your undergraduate education, please provide a brief explanation. If not applicable, enter N/A.
